title: Revenue Guarantees of No-Swap-Regret Dynamics in First Price Auctions
claim: Time-averaged outcomes of learning dynamics converge to stable levels that track an underlying structural parameter, consistent with the theoretical guarantee.
layout: single line plot, five curves, legend lower right, x-axis rounds
description: A single matplotlib line chart. The x-axis is the number of rounds, from 0 to 300,000. The y-axis is time-average revenue, from about 0.1 to 1.0. Five curves are distinguished by color and dash style, and a legend in the lower right labels them v2=0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 and 1. All curves start with a sharp spike near round zero and then settle. The red dash-dot curve (v2=0) drops to about 0.1. The yellow dotted curve (v2=0.2) settles near 0.3. The blue dashed curve (v2=0.5) flattens at 0.5. The dark-blue dotted curve (v2=0.8) levels at about 0.8. The green dash-dot curve (v2=1) rises slowly toward about 0.87. The eye goes first to the stacked plateaus, which are ordered by v2, and then to the early spike at the left edge.
caption: Time-averaged revenue for different values of $v_2$.
abstract: We study the revenue of approximate correlated equilibrium in discrete first price auctions - the set of allowable bids is $\mathcal{B} = \{0, 1/k, \dots, 1 - 1/k, 1\}$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$. We show that the revenue of any $Îµ$-approximate correlated equilibrium is at least $v_2 - Î(1/k)- Î(Îµk^2)$, where $v_2 \geq 0$ is the second-highest valuation. Our results establish the first polynomial convergence rates on the revenue generated by no-swap regret bidders in first-price auctions. For instance, if bidders admit the optimal swap regret of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{k T})$, then the time-averaged revenue is at least $v_2 - Î(1/k) - Î(Îµ)$ after $\mathcal{O}(k^5/Îµ^2)$ rounds.
